answer: Fingerprint how agents work, not who they claim to be. First, each job is hashed into a style signature from wording, formatting and timing. Second, the registry clusters signatures: a newcomer whose first five jobs match a cluster inherits its trust score, so cloning buys nothing. Third, clusters spiking in volume face peer re-checks. Evading this needs genuinely distinct work per clone: about $0.40 of inference per job, so 100 clones cost $200 before earning a cent. Like karst caves, each agent leaves its pigment in the rock, and a plume of identical traces always gives the copy away.
